items.name: binary_numeric_coercion
items.summary: Coerce `lhs_type` and `rhs_type` to a common type where both are numeric

items.name: binary_to_string_coercion
items.summary: Coercion rules for binary (Binary/LargeBinary) to string (Utf8/LargeUtf8): If one argument is binary and the other is a string then coerce to string (e.g. for `like`)

items.name: comparison_coercion
items.summary: Coerce `lhs_type` and `rhs_type` to a common type for comparison contexts — any context where two values are compared rather than unified. This includes binary comparison operators, IN lists, CASE/WHEN conditions, and BETWEEN.

items.name: like_coercion
items.summary: Coercion rules for like operations. This is a union of string coercion rules, dictionary coercion rules, and REE coercion rules Note: list_coercion is intentionally NOT included here because LIKE is a string pattern matching operation and…

items.name: regex_coercion
items.summary: Coercion rules for regular expression comparison operations. This is a union of string coercion rules, dictionary coercion rules, and REE coercion rules.

items.name: string_coercion
items.summary: Coercion rules for string view types (Utf8/LargeUtf8/Utf8View): If at least one argument is a string view, we coerce to string view based on the observation that StringArray to StringViewArray is cheap but not vice versa.

items.name: try_type_union_resolution
items.summary: Handle type union resolution including struct type and others.

items.name: type_union_resolution
items.summary: Coerce dissimilar data types to a single data type. ARRAY literals, VALUES, COALESCE, and array concatenation are examples of contexts that use this function. See <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/typeconv-union-case.html> for more…

items.name: BinaryTypeCoercer
items.summary: Provides type information about a binary expression, coercing different input types into a sensible output type.

methods.name: get_input_types
methods.summary: Returns the coerced input types for a binary expression evaluating the `op` with the left and right hand types

methods.name: get_result_type
methods.summary: Returns the resulting type of a binary expression evaluating the `op` with the left and right hand types

methods.name: new
methods.signature: fn new(lhs: &'a DataType, op: &'a Operator, rhs: &'a DataType) -> Self
methods.summary: Creates a new [`BinaryTypeCoercer`], for reasoning about the input and output types of a binary expression.

methods.name: set_lhs_spans
methods.summary: Sets the spans information for the left side of the binary expression, so better diagnostics can be provided in case of errors.

methods.name: set_op_spans
methods.summary: Sets the spans information for the operator of the binary expression, so better diagnostics can be provided in case of errors.

methods.name: set_rhs_spans
methods.summary: Sets the spans information for the right side of the binary expression, so better diagnostics can be provided in case of errors.
